solutions.title: Business Funding
solutions.headline: Funding for the plans taking shape.
solutions.intro: More demand, a new contract or investment in the business can change how much cash you need. We help you find a useful starting point across borrowing, asset and working-capital options.
solutions.goal: Explore business funding around cash flow, investment and your next commercial move.
uses: Explore invoice finance, loans and revolving facilities around the gap between outgoing costs and incoming payments.
Separate expansion costs from acquisition funding, and test the resulting repayment plan.
Compare the current commitment with replacement funding, including settlement charges and any changes in security.
fit: An operating business with a clear purpose for the funds
A credible repayment case and a view of existing obligations
Decision-makers ready to discuss timing, cost and security
solutions.notFit: A recurring loss without a credible plan needs a different assessment from a temporary cash-flow gap. A pre-revenue company seeking risk capital may need an equity conversation.
solutions.mechanics: A term loan provides borrowing over an agreed period. Revolving credit and overdrafts support changing cash requirements under their own conditions. Invoice finance follows eligible receivables; asset finance relates to equipment. An acquisition may combine debt and equity. Explore each product before comparing the cost and commitments of a proposed facility.
tradeoffs: Total cost
Look beyond the headline rate. Understand interest, arrangement and intermediary fees, any exit charges and the assumptions behind a comparison.
Repayments and flexibility
Match payment dates and duration to cash generation. Clarify early repayment, renewals, increases and what happens if trading changes.
Security and guarantees
A provider may require business security or personal guarantees. Requirements vary; understand the specific exposure before committing.
Assessment and timing
A first response is different from approval or drawdown. Information, credit assessment, documentation and any security arrangements affect the timetable.
prepare: What the funding must achieve
Approximate amount, duration and any important deadline
How the business expects to repay and what it already owes
faqs: Can you help if our bank has declined?

We can discuss the reason for the decision and whether a different structure or provider could be relevant. A previous decline does not rule out every route, but further funding still depends on assessment.
Will I need a personal guarantee?
That depends on the provider, structure and assessment. Any proposed guarantee and its implications need to be made clear before a commitment.
Will an enquiry affect my credit file?
Submitting this enquiry form is not a credit application and does not itself request a credit search. Any later provider application and proposed searches should be explained before you proceed.

solutions.fitIntro: Use these discussion points to frame the requirement. Provider assessment determines suitability, availability and terms.
solutions.valueIntro: You do not need to arrive with a product name. We help clarify where the money is needed and how it will be repaid, then arrange relevant provider introductions with your agreement.

solutions.title: Bridging Loans
solutions.headline: Keep the next step in sight.
solutions.intro: An opportunity and the funds to pursue it do not always arrive together. Explore short-term business funding around the gap, the actual deadline and a credible plan to repay it.
solutions.goal: Short-term funding for a defined business gap, assessed around a credible repayment plan.
uses: Explore the gap before an anticipated investment round, with a clear view of investor progress, remaining conditions and alternative repayment options.
Discuss a bridge to your next raise
Between outgoing costs and incoming cash
Cover a defined timing gap around customer payments, stock, contract delivery or a business transition.
Explore temporary funding for an acquisition, property purchase, equipment investment or refinancing while the next source of capital is arranged.
fit: A business with a specific, temporary funding requirement
An identifiable repayment source and realistic timing
A willingness to review existing borrowing, security and what happens if plans change
solutions.notFit: If the funding gap is ongoing or the repayment source is uncertain, a short-term loan may add pressure. A longer-term funding or equity conversation may be more appropriate.
solutions.mechanics: Bridging describes the purpose of the funding: covering a temporary gap. The actual facility depends on the business, available security and repayment source. A property-backed loan, a short-term business facility and funding between equity rounds can have different terms and assessment requirements. Define the amount, duration and exit first, then establish which structure a provider could consider.
tradeoffs: Repayment and delays
Establish what will repay the loan and when. Test what happens if an investment round, sale, payment or refinance is delayed or does not complete.
The full cost
Compare interest over the expected term alongside arrangement, legal, valuation and exit costs where applicable. Understand any minimum interest period and early repayment terms.
Security and guarantees
Requirements depend on the facility and provider. Understand any business or property security, personal guarantees and the consequences of default before agreeing terms.
Terms and conditions
Review repayment dates, covenants and conditions for releasing funds. Extensions and replacement funding should never be assumed.
prepare: The business purpose, approximate amount and date funds are needed
How long the gap is expected to last and the proposed repayment source
The status of any raise, sale, receivable or refinance and its remaining conditions
Existing borrowing, potential security and a fallback if the expected exit changes
faqs: Can a bridging loan cover the gap before another funding round?

That is a requirement we can discuss. The stage of the raise, investor commitments, conditions and alternative repayment options matter. An anticipated round alone does not establish that a loan is available or suitable.
Is bridging only for property?

No. Businesses can need temporary funding for cash flow, transactions and funding transitions as well as property. The appropriate facility depends on the purpose, repayment source and provider assessment.
How much can we borrow, and how quickly?
The amount, term, cost and timing depend on the business, facility and provider. We start with your requirement and deadline; availability and completion cannot be confirmed before assessment.

solutions.enquiryHeading: What is the gap you need to bridge?

solutions.fitIntro: Start with the amount needed, the period it must cover and the evidence behind repayment. We assess the circumstances with you before identifying a relevant funding route.
solutions.valueIntro: We help set out the gap, the deadline and the proposed exit, then explore relevant provider introductions. A property purchase, a trading requirement and a business awaiting investment need different assessments; we help establish the right starting point.

solutions.title: Property Finance
solutions.headline: Finance the property. Bring the plan to life.
solutions.intro: New premises, a development or a refinance can open the way for your next stage. We help you explore property finance around the asset, the project and how the borrowing will be repaid.
solutions.goal: Funding for commercial premises, property development and refinancing.
uses: Explore commercial mortgages around the property, intended use, deposit and repayment source.
Set out acquisition costs, permissions, build stages, contingency and the proposed sale or refinance.
Review existing borrowing or an equity-release requirement alongside valuation, charges and the replacement terms.
fit: An identifiable property or project and a defined funding purpose
A view of equity, delivery capability and relevant experience
A realistic repayment, sale or refinancing plan
solutions.notFit: A property idea without a worked-through project or exit needs preparation first. This page concerns business property funding, rather than a mortgage for your own home.
solutions.mechanics: A commercial mortgage can support eligible business premises or investment property. Property refinance replaces an existing facility or may release available equity. Development finance is shaped around the site, costs, programme and exit, often with funds released against agreed milestones. A short-term bridge serves a different purpose and needs a credible exit. The asset, borrower and intended use determine which route can be considered.
tradeoffs: Usable funds and your contribution
Clarify the net funds available after costs, the equity contribution and which costs must be met before or alongside lender funds.
Drawdowns and conditions
Understand valuation, monitoring, legal and other conditions, including when money can actually be released.
Interest and fees
Consider the whole project cost, including arrangement, monitoring, legal and exit charges where applicable.
Term and exit
Test sales or refinance assumptions, contingency and what happens if delivery or sales take longer. An extension should not be assumed.
prepare: Property type, region and acquisition or project stage
Costs, equity, planning position and relevant experience
Required date, programme and proposed exit
faqs: Can funding complete by my deadline?
That depends on the asset, available information, valuation, legal work and the provider’s conditions. Share a real deadline early so the critical path can be considered.
How much of our own money will we need?

Your contribution depends on the property, project, provider and costs being funded. Allow for the deposit or equity contribution and any fees, works or other costs that must be paid before funds are released.
Can we refinance a completed development?

A refinance may replace the development facility while a completed property is sold or held. The relevant route depends on the property, income or sale plan, existing borrowing and remaining time before repayment is due.

solutions.usesHeading: What are your plans for the property?
solutions.structureHeading: Match the finance to the stage of the project.
solutions.commitmentsHeading: Equity, drawdowns and the exit plan.

solutions.title: Equity & Growth Capital
solutions.headline: Capital for growth. A new chapter for ownership.
solutions.intro: Grow the company, make an acquisition or change who owns the business. We help you explore equity investment around the opportunity and what it means for the shareholders involved.
solutions.goal: Equity investment for company growth, acquisitions and changes in ownership.
uses: Set out the expansion or acquisition plan and what new investment should enable.
Separate a shareholder sale from capital available to fund the company’s next plans.
Frame the buyout, acquisition or succession objective around management and shareholder alignment.
fit: An established business with a clear growth or ownership event
A credible management team and supporting commercial evidence
Shareholders willing to examine equity and governance trade-offs
solutions.notFit: A pre-revenue startup usually needs a stage-led venture conversation. A short cash-flow gap may be better explored through borrowing than a change in ownership.
solutions.mechanics: New shares can bring capital into the company; a sale of existing shares provides proceeds to selling shareholders. Some transactions combine both. The investment case, valuation, ownership, board rights and future exit expectations need to work together. Established-business growth capital differs from venture investment in an early-stage company, and an acquisition may also use debt.
tradeoffs: Valuation and dilution
Understand the ownership being issued or transferred, how proceeds are used and the effect on existing shareholders.
Governance and control
Board roles, consent rights and other terms can affect decisions even in a minority investment.
Investor alignment
Sector, strategy, management expectations and future funding capacity need to fit the plan.
Process and exit
Investor assessment and shareholder agreements take time. Clarify how long the investor expects to remain involved and how a future sale or other exit might work.
prepare: The intended split between company investment and shareholder proceeds
Current ownership, management involvement and the decisions shareholders can support
Capital purpose, timetable, financial picture and existing advisers
faqs: Does equity always mean selling control?
No, but minority ownership does not mean an absence of governance rights. The proposed terms need specific review.
Is the highest valuation the best offer?
The full agreement matters: governance, conditions, incentives, investor fit and exit expectations can change the overall assessment.
Will you share our information with investors?

We agree the recipients and scope with you before sharing details with a funding provider. Start with a non-confidential outline; detailed ownership records and investor materials can follow through an agreed process.
solutions.fitHeading: A business ready for an ownership decision.
solutions.valueHeading: Bring the growth plan and shareholder goals together.
solutions.preparationHeading: Outline the business and its owners.
solutions.enquiryHeading: What should the next investment make possible?

solutions.fitIntro: An ownership event needs a credible business case and shareholders who can agree what should change. Investor fit and the full terms matter alongside the amount.
solutions.valueIntro: We help clarify where the capital should go, the role of an investor and the ownership priorities behind the transaction. Relevant introductions follow that brief. Investor materials and ownership scenarios can be commissioned separately where preparation is needed.

solutions.title: Venture Funding
solutions.headline: Turn the next milestone into a funding case.
solutions.intro: Build the product, demonstrate demand or scale a working model. We help you connect the next round with the evidence, resources and runway needed to move your company forward.
solutions.goal: Investment for scalable companies, framed around stage, commercial evidence and the next milestone.
uses: Define what still needs proving, the test or customer evidence sought and the cost to reach that point.
Align the milestone, investor proposition, use of proceeds and existing round status.
Show how capital supports delivery or growth, with unit economics, cash burn and later funding in view.
fit: A scalable company with an ambitious but evidenced plan
A defined milestone and a view of runway and future funding
Founders prepared to consider dilution and investor governance
solutions.notFit: Venture capital does not suit every startup. An ordinary working-capital requirement in an established company may be a business-funding conversation.
solutions.mechanics: Venture investment typically involves equity or another investment instrument with its own rights and conditions. The case depends on the company’s stage, team, traction, market and use of funds. Model the capital needed to reach the next milestone and the ownership implications. Equipment finance or a business loan serves a different purpose and still requires its own assessment.
tradeoffs: Investor fit
Investors have different preferences for company stage, sector, geography and round size. A focused approach starts with the evidence your company can show.
Ownership and rights
Consider dilution alongside investor rights, such as board representation, consent over decisions and priority in receiving proceeds. Future rounds can change ownership again.
Runway and milestones
Allow for delays and future capital requirements. A milestone is not a guaranteed valuation increase.
Readiness and execution
Decks, forecasts, ownership and diligence need to tell a coherent story; a raise cannot be guaranteed.
prepare: Stage, customer or technical evidence and what remains unproven
The milestone, costed use of proceeds and runway to reach it
Current round status, existing investor discussions and future capital needs
faqs: Can a pre-revenue business raise capital?
Some investors consider early-stage risk, but the stage, evidence, opportunity and mandate must fit. Pre-revenue status alone does not establish suitability.
How much should we raise?

Start with the cost of the next meaningful milestone and the cash needed to reach it. Allow for fundraising time, delays and a reserve if progress is slower than planned, then consider the ownership implications.
Do I need to upload a pitch deck immediately?
No. A non-confidential summary can establish the initial context before agreeing whether and how more detailed material should be shared.

solutions.valueHeading: Give the vision a clear investment proposition.

solutions.fitIntro: A venture case connects risk, evidence and a scalable opportunity. The round needs a defined milestone and realistic runway; stage, sector, geography and investor mandate must fit the actual company.
solutions.valueIntro: We help explain what the round needs to achieve and why the company is ready for the conversation. We explore relevant investor introductions; financial models and investor materials can be commissioned separately to support the raise.

solutions.title: Complex Funding
solutions.headline: A clear way into a complex funding decision.
solutions.intro: A lender change, an acquisition or an approaching repayment date can bring several decisions together. We help clarify the funding requirement, existing obligations and actions needed to take the case forward.
solutions.goal: A starting point for funding requirements involving unusual structures, deadlines or several stakeholders.
uses: Set out a facility maturity, lender change or refinancing constraint and what must happen next.
Explain the acquisition, carve-out or unusual structure and the stakeholders who need to agree.
Connect a credible operating plan with the immediate constraints and existing obligations.
fit: A clear account of the situation and its underlying business case
Current information and decision-makers able to engage
A realistic plan and willingness to involve appropriate specialists
solutions.notFit: Possible insolvency, imminent enforcement or questions about director duties can require urgent qualified professional advice. New borrowing is not a substitute for resolving an unviable plan.
solutions.mechanics: A complex capital requirement depends on viability, existing obligations, security and stakeholder support. The first task is to establish whether a funding route is realistic and what professional input or consents are needed.
tradeoffs: Viability before capital
Explain how the plan addresses the underlying issue rather than postponing it.
Stakeholder alignment
Existing lenders, shareholders and advisers may need to agree before a transaction can proceed.
Cost and priority
New capital can bring significant cost, security and conditions. These require candid assessment.
Timing and information
Share the deadline and the event behind it. Agree who needs to receive information and how detailed documents will be exchanged before a provider approach.
prepare: What changed, what must happen next and any real deadline
A broad description of the plan, repayment or exit and existing obligations
The stakeholders, advisers and consents involved
faqs: What makes a funding requirement complex?

Several lenders or security interests, a changing ownership structure, an unusual transaction or a tight repayment deadline can all add dependencies. The starting point is a clear account of the situation and a workable business plan.
Should I include detailed creditor information in an enquiry?
Start with a broad, non-sensitive summary. Agree a suitable secure process before sending detailed financial or legal material.
How quickly can the situation be assessed?
That depends on the information, complexity and actual specialist availability. A deadline is important context, not a guarantee of funding by that date.

solutions.fitIntro: The first discussion separates the funding objective from the underlying issue. A viable plan, current information and the real deadline help establish whether a capital conversation is useful.
solutions.valueIntro: We help you explain the commercial plan, existing obligations and decisions that must line up before a provider approach. Where legal, restructuring or insolvency questions arise, appropriately qualified advisers need to lead that work.

solutions.title: Life Sciences
solutions.headline: Capital for the milestone that matters.
solutions.intro: Progress in life sciences depends on evidence, resources and time. We help connect the next scientific or commercial milestone with a clear capital requirement, from development programmes to operating laboratory investment.
solutions.goal: Funding conversations for research, equipment and commercial growth.
uses: Frame the next technical evidence point, remaining uncertainty and resources required.
Connect market evidence, delivery capacity and relevant approval dependencies to the capital plan.
Separate an operating laboratory’s equipment investment from science-led development risk.
fit: A clearly defined scientific or commercial milestone
An appropriate evidence base, team and rights to relevant IP
A realistic budget, runway and view of later capital needs
solutions.notFit: A pre-revenue development business and a profitable laboratory need different funding assessments. Scientific promise alone is not evidence of debt repayment capacity.
solutions.mechanics: Capital for research and development is usually assessed around the company’s stage, evidence and next milestone. A trading laboratory buying equipment has a different requirement, with the asset and repayment capacity central to the discussion. Set out the use of funds before choosing a funding route.
tradeoffs: Milestone and contingency
Allow for development delays and costs beyond the immediate study or validation point.
Capital structure
Consider dilution, repayment and rights over IP in the context of development risk.
Specialist evidence
Provider understanding and relevant diligence matter; Frontier does not independently validate scientific outcomes.
Confidential information
Start with a non-confidential summary. Do not send patient data or unpublished research through an initial enquiry.
prepare: Subsector, current stage and the non-confidential milestone
Evidence already available, resources needed and the broad budget
Timing, runway, later capital needs and relevant specialist dependencies
faqs: Is this only for biotechnology companies?

The starting point is the activity and funding purpose. Research-led companies, diagnostic businesses and operating laboratories can have different needs. Tell us the subsector and stage so the relevant route and specialist input can be established.
Can laboratory equipment be financed separately?
An operating business buying equipment may have a different capital case from a company funding uncertain development. The eligible costs and actual provider scope need to be checked.
Do I need to share confidential research?
Not at first contact. Begin with a non-confidential account of the requirement and agree any later information exchange.

solutions.fitIntro: A development company funding its next evidence point and a trading laboratory buying equipment need different capital. Describe the business, its stage and the purpose of the funds so the discussion starts in the right place.
solutions.valueIntro: We help turn a non-confidential development plan into a clear funding requirement: what the next stage should establish, the budget and the runway needed to get there. Equipment for an operating laboratory may need a different route from research-led growth capital. Specialist scientific and regulatory assessment remains separate.

solutions.title: Technology Finance
solutions.headline: Put better technology behind your plans.
solutions.intro: Modernise systems, automate a process or add new capability. We help you explore funding for the investment while keeping implementation costs and the cash needed to run the business in view.
solutions.goal: Funding for eligible technology equipment and separately assessed software or implementation expenditure.
uses: Define the asset, supplier, delivery and commissioning requirements.
Separate licences, integration, training and ongoing service costs; eligibility depends on the actual facility.
Raising capital for a technology company?
Company fundraising belongs with stage, traction, ownership and runway—not an equipment purchase assessment.
fit: An operating business with a defined purchase or capability investment
A cost breakdown, implementation timetable and credible commercial case
A view of eligible costs, repayment and operating obligations
solutions.notFit: A technology label does not establish eligibility. Software, services and integration costs may be treated differently from equipment; an untested investment needs a credible business case.
solutions.mechanics: Equipment may be considered for hire purchase or leasing, depending on the asset and provider. Software, integration, installation and training can need different treatment. Separate one-off expenditure from ongoing services, and test repayment against delivery and adoption timing. A technology company raising capital for its own growth should explore venture or growth capital rather than treating the round as an equipment purchase.
tradeoffs: Eligible expenditure
Confirm what is actually financeable, including deposits, software, integration and service costs.
Delivery and repayment
Match commitments to installation, adoption and the timing of benefits; do not assume immediate savings.
Ownership and obligations
Clarify ownership or end-of-term options for assets and the conditions of any borrowing.
Company capital
A startup round introduces different ownership, investor and runway considerations from equipment finance.
prepare: The asset or capability, supplier quote and cost categories
Delivery, installation, training and expected productive-use dates
Commercial assumptions, existing obligations and repayment source
faqs: Can software and implementation costs be funded?
That depends on the product and provider. A quote should separate equipment, software, services and implementation so the scope can be assessed.
Will savings cover the repayments?
That is a business-case assumption to test, including delays and downside scenarios. Finance does not guarantee the expected return.
We are a technology startup. Which route should we use?
Start with the company’s stage and capital purpose. The venture or growth-capital journey may be more relevant than an equipment-finance discussion.
solutions.structureHeading: Cost the purchase and the change around it.
solutions.valueHeading: Move from a technology plan to a clear funding requirement.
solutions.enquiryHeading: What will the technology help your business do?
solutions.enquiryIntro: Tell us the project, approximate cost and timing. A supplier quote can follow once we have agreed the scope of the discussion.
solutions.fitIntro: The primary route here is investment by an operating business. A technology company raising growth or venture capital should use the separate company-funding routes.
solutions.valueIntro: We help separate equipment, software, integration and running costs, then explore relevant provider introductions. The funding case should reflect when the technology becomes useful and when the business can support repayments.

solutions.title: Sustainability & Impact
solutions.headline: Put capital behind a more sustainable business.
solutions.intro: Cleaner equipment, more efficient operations or an impact-led growth plan: progress needs a commercial case as well as a clear purpose. We help connect the investment with relevant funding options.
solutions.cta: Discuss your investment or impact plan
solutions.goal: Funding conversations for cleaner operating assets and businesses with an environmental or social purpose.

solutions.notFit: A worthwhile purpose does not automatically establish a repayment or investment case. A green asset is not necessarily an impact investment, grant or discounted loan.
solutions.mechanics: Funding a solar installation or cleaner equipment is different from an investor backing an impact-led company. The capital structure, eligible entity, commercial case and any reporting requirements must be considered separately.
tradeoffs: Commercial viability
Test the investment economics and delivery assumptions alongside the intended benefit.
Evidence and reporting
Clarify the baseline, measurement method and any provider-specific reporting obligations.
Actual product terms
Environmental purpose does not guarantee lower cost, a grant or preferential eligibility.
Measuring results
Allow for installation, adoption and operating conditions when estimating the benefit. Compare actual results with a defined starting point before making claims about savings or impact.
prepare: Operational investment or business-growth purpose and the costed plan
The baseline and intended environmental or social outcome
Delivery assumptions, measurement method and commercial evidence
faqs: Will sustainable finance be cheaper?
Not necessarily. Compare the actual product, terms, requirements and total cost rather than assuming a green label changes the price.
Does this include grants?
This page covers borrowing and investment, rather than a grant service. If grant support is part of your plan, its availability, conditions and any effect on other funding need separate confirmation.
Do we need formal impact reporting?
Requirements vary by route and provider. Measurement should be appropriate to the intended outcome and any actual funding conditions.

Should I connect a wallet or upload identity documents?
No. An initial enquiry should not require wallet connections, private keys, account access or identity documents.
